activity_context.topic_title: The Vector Equation of a Line

feedback.problem: Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through $P(-3,-4,-5)$ and parallel to $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $P$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=p+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $p$ is the position vector of $P.$

In our case, the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -4 \\ -5\end{aligned}].$

Using the formula for the vector equation of a line, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -4 \\ -5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
